summary: First comprehensive horizontal AI regulation. Risk-based framework with prohibited practices, high-risk system duties, general-purpose AI model obligations and transparency rules. Amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (the Digital Omnibus on AI), which deferred the high-risk obligations.
key_provisions: Prohibited practices and AI literacy duties applicable since 2025-02-02
General-purpose AI model obligations applicable since 2025-08-02
Annex III stand-alone high-risk obligations deferred to 2027-12-02
Annex I high-risk obligations embedded in regulated products deferred to 2028-08-02
Penalties up to EUR 35 million or 7 percent of worldwide annual turnover
title: EU AI Act

summary: Sector-led, non-statutory approach relying on existing regulators rather than a dedicated AI regulator. No standalone UK AI act has been enacted. The AI Safety Institute was renamed the AI Security Institute in February 2025.
title: UK AI Regulation Framework

summary: Regulations governing generative AI services offered to the public in China. Emphasizes content control and socialist values.
title: Interim Measures for Generative AI Services

summary: Regulations on algorithmic recommendations in internet services. Requires transparency and user controls.
title: Algorithm Recommendation Regulations

summary: Would have created a risk-based federal AI regime. Bill C-27 died on the Order Paper when Parliament was prorogued on 2025-01-06 and has not been reintroduced. Canada has no comprehensive AI statute in force.
title: Artificial Intelligence and Data Act (AIDA)

summary: Risk-based framework modelled on the EU AI Act. Approved by the Federal Senate on 2024-12-10 and transmitted to the Chamber of Deputies, where it remains in committee. Not yet law.
title: AI Bill (PL 2338/2023)

summary: First intergovernmental standard on AI. Non-binding principles adopted by 46 countries.
title: OECD AI Principles

summary: UN resolution including AI governance provisions, emphasizing international cooperation and capacity building.
key_provisions: AI capacity building for developing nations
title: UN Global Digital Compact (AI Provisions)

summary: G7 framework establishing guiding principles and code of conduct for AI developers.
title: Hiroshima AI Process

summary: First multilateral declaration on frontier AI risk, agreed at the 2023 UK AI Safety Summit. Superseded in practice by a summit series continuing through Seoul, Paris and the 2026 New Delhi AI Impact Summit.
title: Bletchley Declaration
Digital Omnibus on AI — Regulation (EU) 2026/1744
summary: Amends the EU AI Act using fixed calendar dates rather than a conditional trigger. Defers the high-risk obligations, adds two prohibited practices and extends simplifications for smaller providers. Entered into force six days before the original 2026-08-02 high-risk deadline.
key_provisions: Annex III stand-alone high-risk obligations moved to 2027-12-02
Annex I embedded high-risk obligations moved to 2028-08-02
Adds prohibitions on non-consensual intimate imagery and CSAM-generating systems from 2026-12-02
Leaves Article 5 prohibitions, GPAI duties and Article 50 transparency in place

title: Framework Act on the Development of Artificial Intelligence and Establishment of a Foundation for Trust
summary: The world's second comprehensive national AI statute after the EU AI Act. Combines promotion of the domestic AI industry with binding duties for high-impact AI and generative AI, and applies extraterritorially to providers serving the Korean market.
key_provisions: Obligations for high-impact AI in areas such as healthcare, energy and public services
Labelling requirements for generative AI outputs
Additional duties above a training-compute threshold
Extraterritorial application with a domestic representative requirement
Grace period deferring most fines through 2026

title: Act on Promotion of Research, Development and Utilization of AI-Related Technologies
summary: Japan's first AI-specific statute. Promotion-oriented rather than punitive: it sets national coordination machinery and duties to cooperate, but imposes no penalties on developers or deployers.
key_provisions: Establishes an AI Strategy Headquarters led by the Prime Minister
Requires a national AI Basic Plan
Sets cooperation duties for businesses and research institutions

title: Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law (CETS 225)
summary: The first binding international treaty on AI, opened for signature on 2024-09-05. Signatories include the European Union, the United Kingdom and the United States. Not yet in force as of September 2026, pending the required ratifications.
key_provisions: Binding obligations to protect human rights, democracy and the rule of law in the AI lifecycle
Open to non-member states of the Council of Europe
Requires risk and impact management frameworks
Enters into force after five ratifications including three Council of Europe member states

title: Measures for Labeling AI-Generated Synthetic Content
summary: Requires both visible labels and embedded metadata on AI-generated text, images, audio, video and virtual scenes, backed by mandatory national standard GB 45438-2025. Places duties on generating services, distribution platforms and app stores.
key_provisions: Explicit visible labelling of AI-generated content
Implicit labelling embedded in file metadata
Platform duties to verify and preserve labels
User declaration obligations for synthetic content
Backed by mandatory national standard GB 45438-2025
